content:
morgan: FYI RedTeam reported an exposure (RT-42) — audit export presigned URLs were retrievable from outside our VPC. They flagged High. Need repro steps + remediation evidence for retest.

redteam-bot: We POSTed to /admin/export and received a presigned S3 URL, then fetched it from a public IP with no cookies. Example: 
```
curl -v 'https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood-audit-exports/exports/2025-03-01.tar.gz?X-Amz-Algorithm=AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=...'
```
Returned 200 and file contents were the export.

jess: Which code path issues the presign? I think export service uses svc-exporter role. Will grep service/export.go.

rahul: Quick infra note: presign call uses the service account and currently defaults expiry to 7 days (604800s). Also objects are uploaded without explicit SSE-KMS.

alicia: From access logs I can see presign created at 2025-03-01T12:03:21Z (request_id: req-9a1b). GET from IP 18.216.34.12 succeeded at 12:03:24Z.

morgan: Sounds like two problems: TTL too long, and objects not KMS-encrypted. Both increase blast radius.

dana: Compliance perspective: if exported audit data is accessible via long-lived presigned URLs, mark High. It crosses data retention/audit control boundaries.

jess: Proposed quick fixes: 1) reduce presign expiry to 15 minutes (900s), 2) write exported objects with SSE-KMS (customer-managed key), 3) log presign issuer + token id. I'll draft a PR.

morgan: We need reproducible steps and the exact evidence RedTeam can verify post-patch.

rahul: Repro steps for RedTeam (and for our validation):
1) POST /admin/export with admin token (or service token) to create an export.
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/admin/export -d '{"range":"last_30_days"}'
2) In response, copy presigned_url and run from outside our infra:
   curl -I '<presigned_url>'
Expected pre-patch: HTTP/1.1 200 OK and object headers without SSE.
Expected post-patch: HTTP/1.1 403 (if expired) or 200 with header `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms`.

rahul: Logs to collect for validation:
```
# exporter pod
kubectl logs deploy/exporter -c main | grep presign | grep req-9a1b
# S3 metadata
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit-exports --key exports/2025-03-01.tar.gz
```

alicia: I'll pull the prior logs and the S3 head-object output and save as evidence bundle. I'll include request IDs and timestamps (req-9a1b). After PR lands, I'll run the same flow and capture:
- export creation log showing presignExpiry=900
- head-object showing `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms`
- S3 access logs showing denies for external IPs after expiry

redteam-bot: We'll retest once you confirm the patch is deployed. For retest, we'll need the pre/post request IDs and the exact presign_url pattern.

jess: Opening PR now: set defaultPresignTTL=900, enable SSE-KMS on export writer via kms-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01, and add an audit log entry `export.presign_issuer` with token id. Will run canary and roll out.

morgan: Assignments: jess -> PR + rollout, rahul -> review S3 bucket policy + perms, alicia -> collect and upload evidence bundle, dana -> re-evaluate severity after evidence.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-5841 and linked this thread.

morgan: One more ask — when you collect evidence, include the exact curl outputs we expect RedTeam to see so we can close the loop quickly. Keep this thread updated with retest results.
